national-museum-usaf-dayton.name: National Museum of the U.S. Air Force

rows.item: Saturn V: test first stage S-IC-T plus S-II and S-IVB stages of SA-514 (Apollo/Saturn V Center)
rows.notes: Unflown SA-514 upper stages (backup/unflown flight articles) with S-IC-T test first stage. Wikipedia source; museum page not read.

rows.item: Saturn V: unflown flight stages S-IC-14 (SA-514), S-II-15 (SA-515), S-IVB-513
rows.notes: Outdoor/Saturn V Complex at JSC. Stage designations from Wikipedia and apollomaniacs.com; museum page not read.

rows.item: SA-500D dynamic test vehicle (S-IC-D, S-II-F/D, S-IVB-D)
rows.notes: Displayed indoors in the Davidson Center since 2007.
Wikipedia says moved to INFINITY for preservation; public display not confirmed.

rows.item: Saturn IB SA-209 (Skylab rescue / ASTP backup vehicle, never flown)
rows.notes: Restoration finished and returned to Rocket Garden display (space.com). The SA-211 stage display at the Ardmore Alabama welcome center was retired Jan 2023.

rows.item: Final unflown Delta II built from leftover flight hardware (Rocket Garden)
rows.notes: Side boosters and main engine are replicas; rest is genuine unflown program hardware.

rows.item: Booster B1023 (flew Thaicom 8, then Falcon Heavy demo side core), Gateway building
rows.notes: Side booster of the Feb 2018 Falcon Heavy debut.

rows.item: Gemini 5 Titan II GLV first stage segment (s/n 62-12560), Hangar C
rows.notes: Hangar is on a military base; public access can be limited.

rows.item: Restored Convair Atlas D (LV-3B / SM-65D) missile painted as Mercury-Atlas 9, with mock-up Mercury capsule
rows.notes: Authentic Atlas D missile, serial and flown status not stated; it is a missile airframe, not a Mercury-Atlas flight article. Kind is a best guess.

rows.item: R-7 11A511 (Soyuz) built 1984, used as Plesetsk crew-training rocket, mounted on museum building
rows.notes: Real production-built vehicle used as a training unit, equipment removed; museum page says not an actual flight rocket. Operator decides whether it counts.
